title: The Hydrogen Trapping Potential of Cr-rich M23C6 and M7C3 Carbides in Hybrid Steel Alloys Investigated by Atom Probe Tomography
content: Hydrogen is a key element in the transition to a fossil-free society and the application of sustainable technologies. However, the presence of H presents challenges for a lot of materials. Hydrogen gas can dissociate on the material’s surface and be absorbed as atomic H and diffuse into the alloy. H is attracted to high stress areas and promotes crack formation and propagation in these regions. High-strength steels are especially prone to premature failure, which is called hydrogen embrittlement (HE) [1]. One way to prevent detrimental H diffusion is to introduce H traps [2]. Several microstructural features can act as traps and provide different ‘trapping strengths’, usually measured as de-trapping activation energy using thermal desorption mass spectrometry (TDMS). Dislocations and grain boundaries are weak traps and may release H back into the matrix during operation [3]. In contrast, carbides are known as strong H traps that can render H immobile, and thereby preventing its contribution to HE [4], [5], [6].
